stem: Compound T is made by a three-stage synthesis.

parts.label: (a)
(b)(i)
parts.stem:
In stage 2, compound R reacts with ethylamine to form compound S.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}
parts.text: Name the functional group formed in stage 2.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Identify the other product formed in stage 2.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
In stage 3, compound S reacts with a suitable reagent to form compound T.

{{figure:pdf_visual_03.png}}
parts.text: State the formula of a suitable reagent for stage 3.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Name the type of reaction that occurs in stage 3.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem: The relative abundance of the molecular ion peak in the mass spectrum of ethylamine is 62.
parts.text: Calculate the relative abundance of the $M+1$ peak in the mass spectrum of ethylamine.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
The mass spectrum of compound T contains several fragments. The $m/e$ values of two of these fragments are 29 and 91.

Draw the structures of the ions responsible for these peaks.

| $m/e$ | structure of ion |
| :--- | :--- |
| 29 |  |
| 91 |  |

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.stem:
The proton ($^{1}\text{H}$) NMR spectrum of compound T shows hydrogen atoms in different environments. Six of these environments are shown on the structure using letters a, b, c, d, e and f.

{{figure:pdf_visual_04.png}}

Use the letters a, b, c, d, e and f to answer the questions that follow. The questions relate to the proton ($^{1}\text{H}$) NMR spectrum of T.

Proton d does not cause splitting of the peaks for protons c or e under the conditions used.

Each answer may be one, or more than one, of the letters a, b, c, d, e and f.
parts.text: Identify the proton or protons with a chemical shift ($\delta$) in the range 6.0 to 9.0.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text: Identify the proton or protons whose peak will disappear if $\text{D}_2\text{O}$ is added.

parts.label: (e)(iii)
parts.text: Identify the proton or protons whose peak is a triplet.

parts.label: (e)(iv)
parts.text: Identify the proton or protons with the lowest chemical shift ($\delta$).
